Alex: Quick sync — ran the prefetched-KV vs lazy-page-on-demand compare on paged-attn. TL;DR: eager prefetch improves throughput for long-context chat but increases GPU mem pressure and fragmentation. Details below and numbers.

Jin: Bench summary attached (micro-bench harness):
- workload: chat-like, seq=4096, avg prompt ~600 tokens, heater pattern=50% long tail
- eager-prefetch (preload 2x lookahead pages): throughput +18% tokens/s, p99 latency +12%
- lazy-on-demand: throughput baseline, p99 lower but p50 better
GPU util: eager=78% avg, lazy=63% avg.

Sam: Did you see more block-table hotspots with eager? I remember the alloc path locking when multiple requests request adjacent pages.

Jin: Yes — flamegraph shows block-table mutex spikes during prefetch bursts. I/O overlap hides CPU on happy path, but fragmentation (small free runs) increases after sustained prefetch, leading to higher compaction frequency.

Maya: Important interaction: kernel selection (FlashAttention fused vs paged flash variant) changes perf sensitivity. When pages hit in KV (warm), fused FA wins — fewer kernel launches and better occupancy. On misses, paged-FA variant (kernel optimized for scatter gather) recovers better because it overlaps page fetches. So prefetch shifts workload favor to fused path which explains throughput uplift.

Alex: Can you paste the relevant flamegraph snippet / perf numbers?

Jin: Paste: ```
flame: kernel_time  54% fused_fwd
flame: kv_lock      12% block_table::lock
flame: compaction  8% allocator::compact
flame: cuda_memcpy 6% page_fetch
```

Sam: Config/patch I used for the experiment (small diff):
```diff
- kv_paging.strategy = "lazy"
+ kv_paging.strategy = "eager_prefetch"
+ kv_paging.prefetch_lookahead = 2
+ allocator.fragmentation_threshold = 0.15
```

Maya: The allocator.threshold tweak is crucial — without lowering fragmentation_threshold we saw compaction spikes and p99 regressions. Suggest per-shard thresholds: hot shards keep low threshold, cold shards higher to avoid churn.

Sam: Agreed. Also tested a hybrid: start lazy, trigger prefetch for sequences > 1024 tokens or when batch_size >= 8. Hybrid gives most wins: +10% throughput, p99 neutral, less fragmentation.

infra-bot: perf-ci run 3129991110 completed: artifacts -> https://perf.internal/runs/3129991110 (flamegraphs, kernel traces, nvprof)

Alex: Great. Actionable takeaways:
- short term: roll hybrid as opt-in flag behind experiment, set per-shard allocator thresholds.
- mid term: reduce block-table lock contention: investigate sharded block-table (per-page-range locks) or lock-free freelist for allocator.
- kernel-level: add a tiny heuristic in kernel selector: if page-miss-rate > 8% prefer paged-FA optimized path.

Maya: I can draft the kernel-selector heuristic + perf guardrail. Also will sketch sharded block-table RFC.

Jin: I'll export perf artifacts and a compact regression report. Will include nvprof timelines showing overlap benefits for eager prefetch.

Sam: I'll put the hybrid rollout flag behind `kv.paging.mode = "hybrid-experiment"` and add telemetry: page_hit_rate, compaction_events, block_lock_ms.

Alex: Cool. Owners: Maya (kernel-selector + RFC), Sam (rollout flag + telemetry), Jin (bench artifacts + regression writeup). Ping back by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
